subject: Cert escrow & FQDN ownership — legal review and ops ask
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Acme Finance <security@acme.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-30T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Cert escrow & FQDN ownership — legal review and ops ask

Hi Janet / Acme security team,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we prepare the private deployment of Redwood Private into Acme's VPC, two items came up that we need to resolve before we can start generating customer-facing certificates for the private endpoints:

1) Certificate escrow / key custody model (required by Acme for disaster recovery and audit).
2) Clear ownership mapping for the set of FQDNs that will terminate on Redwood-managed gateways and sidecars.

Attached is a first-pass list of the FQDNs we think are in scope (fqdns-in-scope.csv). High level options we can support:

- Option A: Redwood-managed certificates with KMS/HSM-backed key escrow. Keys are stored encrypted in customer-dedicated KMS with split-access (customer legal retains approval), retrieval requires an escrow agreement and audit triggers; we can provide signed audit logs and notarized retrieval events.
- Option B: Customer-provided CA / offline root. Acme runs the root CA and issues leaf certs via CSR flow to Redwood. Redwood will store only the leaf certs; private keys never leave customer HSM. We provide rotation/CSR tooling and documented proof-of-possession checks.

We need two asks of the Acme team to move forward:
- Legal: a short escrow clause or confirmation of acceptable custody model (Option A vs Option B). If Option A, we'll share a limited-scope escrow agreement for DocuSign.
- Ops/SRE: confirmation of which option Acme prefers and any rotation frequency constraints.

If helpful, we can propose hybrid: Redwood stores an encrypted backup of keys in customer-managed KMS (customer-owned key) but key release is gated by DocuSign-signed escrow release.

Can you please have legal or security confirm which model they prefer and any mandatory language? We can follow up with a one-page escrow agreement and the technical runbook.

Regards,

Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: fqdns-in-scope.csv (text/csv)]

From: Janet Lowe <janet.lowe@acme.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Finance <security@acme.com>
Date: 2027-01-30T09:34:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cert escrow & FQDN ownership — legal review and ops ask

Thanks, Kimberly — good summary. Our security and legal teams reviewed the two options and have initial concerns:

- Option A (Redwood-managed escrow): Legal is hesitant about any arrangement where a vendor holds private keys for production certs, even if encrypted. They'll accept an immutable, auditable escrow only if the escrow contract limits use to "recovery only", requires two-party sign-off, and guarantees deletion after rotation or on contract termination.
- Option B (Customer CA): Preferred from a risk perspective, but our infra team needs automation for CSR/rotation — we cannot run manual CSR workflows. We need a documented automation path and signed proof-of-possession/nonce exchange.

Attached is a draft escrow clause from our counsel and a redline we started on the contract (acme-escrow-contract-draft.pdf). Can Redwood produce:

1) A one-page operations runbook that shows how Option B automation would work end-to-end (CSR flow, rotation window, rollback, and proof-of-possession).
2) If you prefer Option A, a proposed escrow agreement (DocuSign-ready) that includes the two-party release requirement and deletion guarantee after rotation.

Janet Lowe
Director, Security Engineering
Acme Finance
[Attachment: acme-escrow-contract-draft.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Internal — forwarding Acme's reply (below) and next steps.

---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Janet Lowe <janet.lowe@acme.com>
Date: Sat, Jan 30, 2027 at 9:34 AM
Subject: Re: Cert escrow & FQDN ownership — legal review and ops ask
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Finance <security@acme.com>

[see attached redline and draft clause]

----------------------------------------

Proposed actions:
- Karthik: can you produce a 2-page runbook for Option B (customer CA + automated CSR flow) by EOD Monday? Include: CSR sequence, nonce proof-of-possession, rotation cadence (default 90d), rollback steps, telemetry we emit (audit events), and a sample "proof-of-possession" API exchange. Also include the storage model (we store only leaf certs, no private key).
- Marissa: confirm if we can guarantee rotation windows and a deletion workflow that meets Acme's "deletion after rotation/termination" clause. If there are SLOs (e.g., 24h window to rotate after root expiry), flag them.
- Legal: I'll start a short escrow agreement template for Option A but mark it as high friction; only propose if Acme's legal insists. That template must include two-party release and explicit deletion guarantee.

Notes and considerations:
- For Option A: we can implement encrypted key escrow where keys are wrapped by a customer-owned KMS key (customer-supplied ARN) and stored in our encrypted blob store. Retrieval requires DocuSign-signed release + internal approval workflow + audit log. That's the hybrid path Kimberly mentioned.
- For Option B: need to ensure our deployment automation supports an offline root and periodic rotation without human-in-the-loop. This affects bootstrap on air-gapped / on-prem installs.

I'll draft the runbook outline and share in INF-4123; Karthik please add the sequence diagrams.

Thanks,
Kimberly

[Attachment: acme-escrow-contract-draft.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-31T15:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Cert escrow & FQDN ownership — legal review and ops ask

Quick note — agree we should push Option B as the default (customer-owned CA) unless Acme's legal absolutely requires escrow. If escrow is required, we only accept a customer-owned KMS-wrapped escrow with DocuSign release gates and a documented deletion flow.

Karthik: include in the runbook a) proof-of-possession handshake details, b) HSM/KMS wrap model for escrow backups, c) how we log and store retrieval events for audit.

Also add a short checklist in the runbook so our Solutions team can use it during the onboarding call (who signs, which FQDNs, expected rotation cadence, who holds the root).

I'll loop in Legal to expedite the DocuSign template if needed.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
